name: Elliot Cotton
life: “I still remember seeing an old relationship turned into a scene onstage.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Elliot by a small Monday habit. Elliot checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I am the brother's former girlfriend. There is a paragraph I never wanted my child to read.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Elliot has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with auburn hair cut square at the nape. Elliot turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Elliot never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Elliot can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To protect the child's privacy around the old relationship.
family: Martin Martin is Elliot’s half-sibling. Elliot chooses whether to use it. Martin saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Martin says, “I promised a recording to my sister overseas.”
connections: Leona Navarro. The private reading gives someone portrayed in the book a place to raise concerns before publication.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the manuscript returned unopened
reactions.response: Elliot returns the pages privately without treating keeping them closed as a verdict on the work.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Elliot keeps listening through the pause and lets the musician choose the next note.

reactions.situation: When a relative hints at needing company
reactions.response: Elliot may initially offer a repair, but sits down as soon as the request becomes clear.
